papers.title_en: Fault-Tolerant Design and Multi-Objective Model Checking for Real-Time Deep Reinforcement Learning Systems
papers.authors: Guoxin Su, Thomas Robinson, Hoa Khanh Dam, Li Liu, David S. Rosenblum
papers.evidence: 实时控制系统的容错设计
papers.tldr: 针对实时深度强化学习（DRL）系统在延迟等故障下的可靠性挑战，本文提出一种形式化框架，用于设计和分析DRL代理与备用控制器之间的切换机制。研究通过时间自动机建模并转换为马尔可夫决策过程，利用创新的多目标模型检测技术在保证硬安全约束的同时优化性能。此外，开发的GPU加速工具MOPMC在处理大规模模型和多目标优化时展现出卓越的扩展性。
papers.abstract_en: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for solving complex decision-making problems. However, DRL-based systems still face significant dependability challenges particularly in real-time environments due to the simulation-to-reality gap, out-of-distribution observations, and the critical impact of latency. Latency-induced faults, in particular, can lead to unsafe or unstable behaviour, yet existing fault-tolerance approaches to DRL systems lack formal methods to rigorously analyse and optimise performance and safety simultaneously in real-time settings. To address this, we propose a formal framework for designing and analysing real-time switching mechanisms between DRL agents and alternative controllers. Our approach leverages Timed Automata (TAs) for explicit switch logic design, which is then syntactically converted to a Markov Decision Process (MDP) for formal analysis. We develop a novel convex query technique for multi-objective model checking, enabling the optimisation of soft performance objectives while ensuring hard safety constraints for MDPs. Furthermore, we present MOPMC, a GPU-accelerated software tool implementing this technique, demonstrating superior scalability in both model size and objective numbers.
